note: HISTORICAL annual total returns (percent), rounded to one decimal. These are records of the past used only for stress tests; they are never a forecast. Figures follow widely published annual series (S&P 500 total return, 10-year US Treasury total return, 3-month T-bill, CPI-U Dec-Dec) and may differ slightly between publishers. Users can add their own custom scenarios.

scenarios.name: Great Depression (1929-1932)
scenarios.plain: The worst stock market crash in US history, with falling prices (deflation).

scenarios.name: 1970s stagflation (1973-1974)
scenarios.plain: Stocks fell sharply while prices rose very fast.

scenarios.name: Dot-com bust (2000-2002)
scenarios.plain: Three losing years in a row for stocks; bonds did well.

scenarios.name: Global financial crisis (2008)
scenarios.plain: Stocks lost more than a third of their value in one year.

scenarios.name: Inflation shock (2022)
scenarios.plain: Stocks and bonds both fell in the same year while prices jumped.
